xBRIEFInfo.description: Spike: tag page Actors tab lists wrong actors

plan.title: SPIKE: tag page's Actors tab lists actors from matching videos, not actors matching the tag

narratives.Overview: Opening an actor tag shows videos where any actor in the film matches the tag - correct. But the Actors tab lists EVERY actor appearing in those films, not only the actors who match the tag.
narratives.Problem:
Not cosmetic. On a large library a tag matching a handful of performers can return a tab listing hundreds of unrelated ones, which makes the tab actively misleading rather than merely noisy.

The shape is clear - the actor list is almost certainly derived from the filtered ASSETS rather than from the TAG - but the deriving code was not located and must not be guessed at.
narratives.Action:
SPIKE FIRST: locate the derivation. Then make the Actors tab mean 'actors matching this tag'.

The Videos tab answers 'what can I watch'; the Actors tab must answer 'who is this tag about'. Deriving actors from video results conflates the two.
narratives.Constraint: The same tab exists for studios and plain tags. If the derivation is shared, the fix AND its test must cover all of them, not only actors.
narratives.Risk: A shared derivation means a narrow fix silently leaves the other entity types wrong.
narratives.Test: T5 - for a tag matching 2 of 5 actors in a film, the Actors tab returns exactly 2. Covers studios and plain tags if the derivation is shared.

items.title: Locate the actor derivation for the tag page
Determine whether studios and plain tags share it
Derive actors from the tag, not from filtered assets
T5 across every entity type that shares the derivation
